claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 19 and he's still in sixth form doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful. Since Alex is 19 and still in approved education (A-levels in sixth form), he can potentially qualify for Child Benefit.

Let me ask you the next question:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's an important requirement met.

Now I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex? This means either you live with him, or you're paying at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards looking after him (for example, on food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that.

One more question to complete the assessment:

**Do you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000 per year?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I need to mention something - Alex's other parent also lives with him and they already claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that important information. That actually changes the situation significantly.

Under the Child Benefit rules, **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child**. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to claim for the same child.

If you believe you should be the one receiving Child Benefit instead, you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss changing who claims for Alex. However, if both parents are in agreement that the other parent should continue to claim, then you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me confirm: **Are there any other children that you are responsible for that we should assess?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on the information you've provided, I can now give you my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

You are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex because another person is already claiming for him. While Alex would ordinarily qualify (being under 20 and in approved education), the rules state that only one person can receive Child Benefit for each child.

If you'd like to discuss changing who claims for Alex, you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office directly to work through this with them and the other parent.
